title: Sum Up To N
prompt: solve(n) should return the sum of all integers from 1 to n (inclusive). It's returning the wrong total.
hint: Check the loop's stopping condition against what 'inclusive' means.

title: Find The Match
prompt: solve(items, target) returns the first item strictly equal to target, or null if none match. It's matching things it shouldn't.
hint: Assignment and comparison look similar but do very different things in JavaScript.

title: Delayed Greetings
prompt: solve(names) returns an array of index-to-name pairs like '0: Ann', built by scheduling each line with a callback (simulated here with a synchronous queue, not setTimeout, so it stays testable). Every line currently shows the same, wrong index.
hint: var is function-scoped, not block-scoped -- every closure captured the same variable.

title: Fetch Then Use
prompt: solve(id) should look up a user (simulated async lookup) and return their formatted name. It currently returns garbage because it uses the result before it's ready.
hint: userPromise is a Promise object, not the resolved value -- what keyword unwraps it?

title: Remove Evens
prompt: solve(nums) should return the array with all even numbers removed (mutating in place is fine, return the same array). It skips some evens when there are two in a row.
hint: splice shifts every later element down by one -- what happens to i on the next iteration?

title: Factorial
prompt: solve(n) should return n! (factorial). Right now it blows the call stack.
hint: Every recursive function needs a condition where it stops calling itself.

title: Fibonacci
prompt: solve(n) returns the nth Fibonacci number (0-indexed: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8...). It's off by one term.
hint: Compare the recursive calls to the definition: each term needs the two before it.

title: Is It A Palindrome
prompt: solve(str) returns true if str reads the same forwards and backwards, ignoring case. Mixed-case palindromes are failing.
hint: Case-sensitivity is silently breaking the comparison for anything but all-lowercase input.

title: Double Every Item
prompt: solve(nums) should return a new array with every number doubled. It's returning an array of undefined.
hint: A callback that computes a value still needs to hand that value back.

title: Last Element
prompt: solve(arr) should return the last element of the array. It's grabbing undefined instead.
hint: Arrays are zero-indexed -- what's the highest valid index for a given length?

title: Fetch In Order
prompt: solve(ids) should fetch each id (simulated, out-of-order latency) and return names in the SAME order as ids, not in whichever order they resolve.
hint: forEach doesn't wait for its async callbacks, and doesn't preserve arrival order either -- what tool runs promises in parallel but keeps their order?

title: Countdown
prompt: solve(n) should return an array counting down from n to 1, e.g. solve(3) -> [3,2,1]. As written it never terminates.
hint: The loop variable needs to move toward the stopping condition, not away from it.
